newsitem.title: USA: Killer of German tourist in Miami pleads guilty.
newsitem.headline: Killer of German tourist in Miami pleads guilty.

text.p: A Florida teenager avoided a possible death sentence by pleading guilty on Friday to the 1993 murder of a German tourist, one of a spate of killings that tarnished the state's image as a tourist mecca.
Damon Peterson, 19, was sentenced to life in prison and will spend a minimum of 25 years behind bars before becoming eligible for parole, said Dade County Assistant State Attorney Anita Gay.
Peterson pleaded guilty to shooting German tourist Jorg Schell in the neck outside a hotel in Homestead, Florida, south of Miami, on March 11, 1993.
Two other men charged in the robbery-murder were scheduled for trial in December but were reported to be considering plea deals.

Peterson also pleaded guilty to an attempted robbery charge in the Schell slaying, as well as armed robbery and several other counts in connection with an attack on a Connecticut woman the day after the murder.
The killing was one of a series of 1993 attacks on foreign tourists that tarnished Florida's international tourism image and put a damper on a $32-billion-a-year industry.
The slayings prompted state officials to improve street lighting, post signs guiding tourists away from unsafe areas and post guards at highway rest stops.
